title: Filing and practice returns
blurb: Ways to file, then two practice returns on your own.

levels.title: Ways to file a return
learn: Name the ways to file a return and say what NETFILE is.
Tell the filing deadline from the payment deadline.

cards.text: You can file your own return, or have someone else file it. Your own: tax software, SimpleFile or a paper tax return. Someone else: a professional tax preparer or a volunteer at a free tax clinic.

Tax software that the CRA has certified helps you work out your tax and send your return electronically. NETFILE is the CRA service that carries your return from that software to the CRA over the internet. Software first, then NETFILE.

image.alt: An open laptop with a blank screen beside a stack of blank forms

cards.text: For the 2025 return, NETFILE is open from February 23, 2026 until January 29, 2027. With a paper return, you include one copy of each information slip. SimpleFile is for people the CRA invites. It is one of the ways you file your own return, and it files the return for you automatically, for free.

image.alt: A blank form with a blank slip clipped to it and an envelope

cards.text: A tax preparer, such as an accountant, prepares your return and sends it to the CRA for a fee, using a service called EFILE. A free tax clinic is run by volunteers. They complete returns for people with a modest income and a simple tax situation.

image.alt: Two desks with blank forms and pencils and an empty chair at each

cards.text: Filing and paying each have a deadline. Most people file by April 30 of the year after the tax year, so for the 2025 return that is April 30, 2026. Here are the dates for the 2025 return.

figure.title: Deadlines for the 2025 return
rows: Deadline to file if you or your partner is self-employed

cards.text: Students, even with little income, should file every year to get the benefit and credit payments they qualify for. A tax discounter is something else: a business that pays you cash now for a refund still to come, then collects the refund itself. It pays you less than the refund.

levels.title: Practice return: Marcus
learn: Work a whole return on your own, one step at a time.
Say why a return with $0 tax still gets filed.

cards.text: This return is for the 2025 tax year, the same year the tax program your class uses files in December.

image.alt: A calendar page with empty squares, a pencil, a notebook and a blank card

cards.text: Marcus is a student who worked at a coffee shop for five months. He has a T4 and a T4A for other income, in box 028. His T4A has no tax taken off. The amounts are made up. Here are his slips.

You work the return in this order. Marcus has no RRSP, so that step is $0. After taxable income come net federal tax, Alberta tax after credits, total tax, tax withheld, and then the refund or balance owing.
His CPP deduction is $71.42. The first federal bracket is 14.5% up to $57,375. Alberta's is 8% up to $60,000. A credit lowers tax but cannot take it below $0. His Alberta credits total $1,825.40.

The employer took income tax off Marcus's pay. If his tax is less than what was withheld, the difference comes back as a refund, and his return is where it shows. The CRA says to do your taxes every year to get the benefit and credit payments you are eligible for.

image.alt: An open envelope with gold discs on it and a folded blank form

levels.title: Practice return: Amara
learn: Work a harder return: two T4s and a T5.
Explain why a person with two jobs can owe tax.

cards.text: Amara changed jobs in July, so she has two T4s. She also has a T5 from her bank. She has no RRSP, so that step is $0. Her one return puts all of this together. The amounts are made up.
Follow the same steps as before. Her CPP deduction, line 22215, is $310. All her taxable income is in the first brackets: 14.5% federal and 8% Alberta. Round each tax to the nearest cent.

image.alt: Three wooden blocks of rising height with a ruler, a pencil and a notepad

cards.text: Here are the credits her return uses. A credit lowers tax but cannot take it below $0. Alberta's credits here are the basic personal amount, CPP and EI.

Each employer figured her tax as if its job were her only job. Each used a full set of basic claims, such as the basic personal amount. Her return counts all her income together and uses the basic personal amount once.

image.alt: Two small labelled jars with gold discs and a larger empty jar between them

cards.text: When the tax withheld is less than the total tax, the difference is a balance owing, on line 48500. A refund is line 48400. For the 2025 return, the deadline to pay tax owing was April 30, 2026.
